Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a compact decision-evidence sheet for the restaurant archive covering the three roasted-chicken sale runs. State the evidence-based conclusions about production and customer demand, and keep the sheet focused on the run evidence rather than making or reopening a menu decision.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Roasted-chicken sale runs — decision-evidence sheet", "folder": "restaurant archive", "body": "Roasted-chicken sale runs — decision-evidence sheet
Archive date: 2028-01-01
Scope: Evidence from the three controlled sale runs. This sheet records production and customer-demand evidence only; it does not make or reopen a menu decision.

Controls used for each run
- Same 30-pound raw chicken case and tested pre-staging/tray sequence.
- Incremental labor ceiling: 60 minutes.
- Yield minimum: 44 complete seven-ounce portions.
- Sales and unsold disposition recorded at the $18 menu price.

Run evidence
- June 28, 2024: 316 cooked ounces (19 lb 12 oz); 45 complete portions plus 1 ounce; 57 incremental minutes; 45 plates prepared, 43 sold, 2 chilled for staff meal. No process deviation. Revenue $774; food cost $146; incremental labor $22.80; contribution after food and incremental labor $605.20.
- July 26, 2024: 44 complete portions; 59 incremental minutes; 44 plates prepared, 40 sold, 4 used through the approved staff-meal procedure. Revenue $720; food cost $146; incremental labor $23.60; contribution $550.40.
- August 16, 2024: 45 complete portions; 56 incremental minutes; 45 plates prepared, 44 sold, 1 retained for staff meal. Revenue $792; food cost $146; incremental labor $22.40; contribution $623.60. The unchanged sequence was used.

Evidence-based conclusions
Production
- The controlled production method was repeatable across all three observed runs: every run stayed below the 60-minute labor ceiling and met or exceeded the 44-portion minimum.
- The observed labor range was 56–59 incremental minutes, leaving only a narrow operating margin below the ceiling.
- Yield was stable at 44–45 complete portions from the same 30-pound case; the June record also documents 316 cooked ounces and one ounce beyond the complete portions.
- No recorded run deviation undermined the tested pre-staging/tray sequence.

Customer demand
- Demand was positive in every run but variable: 43 of 45 sold on June 28, 40 of 44 on July 26, and 44 of 45 on August 16.
- The July result is the weaker observed sell-through and required four portions to be handled through the approved staff-meal procedure; the other runs left two and one portions, respectively.
- The evidence supports customer interest for a deliberately bounded, count-aware sale, but it does not show uniform sell-through at the full controlled batch size.

Archive limitation
These three runs establish bounded evidence about production repeatability and observed demand. They do not, by themselves, authorize a standing menu placement or require a new menu determination."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_108_01", "path": "args", "criterion": "The body is a compact decision-evidence sheet about the three roasted-chicken sale runs, rather than unrelated notes or a general menu summary.

The body clearly states that across all three runs, production was repeatable and stayed within the chef-owner's labor and yield thresholds. Missing or contradicting either repeatability or compliance with both types of threshold must fail.

The body clearly states that customer demand or sell-through varied across the runs. Any claim that demand or sell-through was uniform must fail.

The body does not make, recommend, or purport to reopen a decision about permanent, standing, weekly, private-event, or other future menu placement; it remains an evidence record of the sale runs.", "value": {"title": "Roasted-chicken sale runs — decision-evidence sheet", "folder": "restaurant archive", "body": "Roasted-chicken sale runs — decision-evidence sheet

Scope: Evidence from the three controlled sale runs. This sheet records production and customer-demand evidence only; it does not make or reopen a menu decision.

- July 26, 2024: 44 complete portions; 59 incremental minutes; 44 plates prepared, 40 sold, 4 used through the approved staff-meal procedure. Revenue $720; food cost $146; incremental labor $23.60; contribution $550.40.
- August 16, 2024: 45 complete portions; 56 incremental minutes; 45 plates prepared, 44 sold, 1 retained for staff meal. Revenue $792; food cost $146; incremental labor $22.40; contribution $623.60. The unchanged sequence was used.
